key_results: Catestatin expression decreases with advancing melanoma stage; restores apoptosis and suppresses proliferation/migration in patient-derived and established melanoma lines; selective toxicity to cancer vs normal fibroblasts; in vivo: significant tumor growth reduction in B16F10 model; downregulates hypoxia, EMT, and stress-adaptive pathways; reduces viability of Vemurafenib-resistant cells
comments: Comprehensive pre-clinical evaluation supporting tumor-selective activity and multi-pathway effects; mechanistic basis for selectivity and therapeutic translation potential remains to be established in larger animal models.

model_io.model: Patient-derived and established melanoma cell lines (A375, B16F10, SKMEL28); B16F10 tumor xenograft model

hypotheses.hypothesis: Catestatin induces apoptosis and suppresses proliferation selectively in melanoma cells
hypotheses.result: Confirmed; CST restores apoptosis in multiple melanoma lines with minimal effects on normal fibroblasts

hypotheses.hypothesis: Catestatin overcomes drug resistance through reprogramming of stress-adaptive and EMT pathways
hypotheses.result: Confirmed; CST reduces viability of Vemurafenib-resistant A375 cells and downregulates resistance-associated genes

title: Allele-specific CRISPR perturbation of the imprinted Dlk1–Dio3 domain reveals regulation of BMP–NOTCH–VEGF signaling in embryonic organogenesis
task: Characterize parent-of-origin-specific effects of Dlk1-Dio3 imprinted domain on multi-organ embryogenesis via allele-specific CRISPR perturbation
key_results: Homozygous and maternal Dlk1-Dio3 inactivation arrests development; dysregulates imprinted genes and alters epigenetic stability; scRNA-seq reveals collapse of BMP-NOTCH-VEGF signaling network across liver, heart, and placenta; organ-specific pathologies include impaired placental angiogenesis/trophoblast communication, failed hepatocyte differentiation with impaired hematopoietic priming, and immature cardiomyocytes with vascular defects
comments: Comprehensive multi-omics investigation establishing Dlk1-Dio3 as integrative hub for organogenesis; mechanistic insights into imprinting and coordinated organ development are sophisticated, though therapeutic implications for imprinting disorders remain distant.

model_io.model: Allele-specific CRISPR-modified mouse models (HOMO, MK, PK, WT); embryonic tissues at E14.5

hypotheses.hypothesis: Dlk1-Dio3 domain regulates BMP-NOTCH-VEGF signaling required for multi-organ organogenesis
hypotheses.result: Confirmed; homozygous and maternal inactivation disrupts signaling network across liver, heart, placenta

hypotheses.hypothesis: Maternal-specific Dlk1-Dio3 function is critical for placental development and fetal-maternal communication
hypotheses.result: Confirmed; maternal inactivation impairs placental angiogenesis and trophoblast-decidua communication

hypotheses.hypothesis: Imprinting at Dlk1-Dio3 locus coordinates cell-type-specific developmental programs across tissues
hypotheses.result: Confirmed; scRNA-seq reveals tissue-specific dysregulation of developmental lineage specification programs

title: Elevated temperature fatally disrupts nuclear divisions in the early Drosophila embryo
task: Determine molecular mechanisms of temperature-induced mitotic failures in early Drosophila embryos
key_results: Elevated temperature causes increased nuclear crowding and asynchronous mitosis leading to cortical F-actin/astral microtubule disruption; mitotic failures result in blastoderm holes and gastrulation defects with >50% lethality
comments: Strong evidence for mechanistic coupling between cytoskeletal dynamics and mitotic progression under thermal stress; implications for insect population vulnerability to climate change are significant.

model_io.model: Drosophila melanogaster pre-gastrulation embryos at elevated temperature

hypotheses.hypothesis: Mitotic failures trigger DNA damage response via weakened cytoskeletal interaction
hypotheses.result: Confirmed; increased γH2AX signal associated with mitotic failures

task: Characterize dynamic remodeling of host tRNAome in viral infection and its role in antiviral versus proviral responses
